questions: Did this patient suffer a sudden collapse or acute neurological event (such as a stroke) prior to admission?
Was there a recent head injury or fall that caused the head bandage?
Did the patient undergo recent brain or cranial surgery?
Is the patient currently conscious and able to follow simple commands?
Is the device around the neck a tracheostomy tube?
Does the patient have a known brain tumor or malignancy?
Has the patient had a recent infection such as meningitis or encephalitis?
Has the patient had a recent cardiac arrest or hypoxic event?
Is there a ventricular drain or shunt in place?
Has the patient been having seizures?
Was therapeutic hypothermia/targeted temperature management used after the cardiac arrest?
Does the patient show any signs of brainstem reflexes (e.g., pupillary light reflex, corneal reflex)?
Has an EEG been performed, and if so, did it show severe diffuse slowing or burst-suppression?
Are the limbs showing decorticate or decerebrate posturing, or are they flaccid?
Are the pupils fixed and dilated, and is there no pupillary response to light?
Is there no corneal reflex when the cornea is touched?
Is there no gag reflex or cough reflex with tracheal suctioning?
Does the patient still have spontaneous respiratory effort (gasping or breathing movements)?
How long has it been since the cardiac arrest (more than 24 hours)?
Is the patient completely dependent on mechanical ventilation with no spontaneous breathing?
Has an apnea test been performed, and if so, was there no respiratory effort?
Is the body temperature currently normal (not hypothermic)?
Is systolic blood pressure above 100 mmHg without vasopressor support?
Was the cardiac arrest the primary cause of the current neurological state, or did it happen in a patient with a pre-existing chronic neurological condition?
Is the patient's current state consistent with a chronic vegetative or minimally conscious state?
Does the patient have a known diagnosis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) or motor neuron disease?
How long has the patient been bedridden with a tracheostomy (more than 1 month)?
Has the patient been gradually deteriorating over weeks to months, with progressive muscle wasting and weakness?
Does the patient have a diagnosis of advanced dementia (e.g., severe Alzheimer's disease) prior to the cardiac arrest?
Was the patient living in a long-term care facility or nursing home before this admission?
Did the patient have severe pre-existing comorbidities such as end-stage renal disease, advanced heart failure, or terminal cancer before the cardiac arrest?
Was the cardiac arrest unwitnessed with prolonged downtime before resuscitation?
